changes.finding: BC Builds: passes the published items this screen checks: non-residential space is 0.0% of area, under the 30% cap; ground must break within 12 to 18 months of the conditional land contribution letter. BC Builds works opportunity by opportunity; middle-income rents and the team's capacity are not assessed here.

12 storeys puts the building under Part 3 of the BC Building Code 2024 and the Vancouver Building By-law 2025; wood frame is standard to 6 storeys and encapsulated mass timber is permitted to 18 under the VBBL; seismic changes apply to permits from 2026-09-15.

Community Housing Fund: whether it meets the criteria cannot be confirmed without the land tenure (lease of at least 60 years at nominal value, or ownership). Unit mix matches 30/50/20 within tolerance; site control (finalized) meets the readiness bar; construction must be able to start within 18 months of award. Its 2025 call did not proceed (February 2026), so no intake is open now; the program page says it will post when next seeking proposals (as of 22 Sep 2026).
BC Housing minimum net unit areas are studio 33, one-bedroom 49, two-bedroom 67, three-bedroom 86 m²; the option averages 80 m² gross per unit, so net areas should be checked at the plan stage.

Would be a program for this housing if it is Indigenous-led, or partnered with an Indigenous housing provider or Nation (not said on the option): affordable rental homes for Indigenous families, Elders, individuals and people with disabilities, on and off reserve; every home rent geared to income (fixed rents may be considered on reserve). It funds building the homes (the Province's funding programs page: "funding to build and to support the creation of" them). A project enters by BC Housing's request for proposals. No intake is open now (closed: no call is posted on the program page (read 23 Nov 2026)). Its homes are all rent geared to income; this option has 36 market-rent homes, which it would not carry. Its criteria are not tested here.

Would be a program for this housing if it is for women, gender-diverse people and children leaving violence (not said on the option): housing with supports for women and their children who are at risk of, or have experienced, violence, in four streams: safe homes (stays of about 10 days), transition houses (about 30 days), second-stage housing (up to about 18 months) and long-term rental housing. It funds 1,500 new homes from 2018, and the service agreement each provider runs them under. A project enters by agreement with BC Housing: the framework names no application route, so ask BC Housing. The building is owned by the Provincial Rental Housing Corporation for the buildings and land created under the fund, leased to non-profit societies and co-operatives. Rents: 30% of income in second-stage and long-term rental housing, by BC Housing's rent scale; a resident on income assistance pays the maximum shelter component. Intake: not stated on the program page (read 23 Nov 2026). Its criteria are not tested here.

A program for this kind of housing (independent rental): a federal Crown corporation that brings financing, land and partnerships to affordable housing; it counts housing as affordable at no more than 30% of a household's before-tax income. It funds flexible financing, land and partnerships; no application terms were read. A project enters not stated on the page read; CMHC's Affordable Housing Fund page directs organizations to it. Intake: not stated on the page read (23 Nov 2026). Its criteria are not tested here.
Residential floor area 9,600 m² is within sub-area B's 23,600 m², the most the by-law allows there (FSR 2.46 on 3,908.0 m²).
Height 36.6 m is within the outright maximum of 91.0 m.
Not for this option: the program takes non profit society or housing cooperative proponents, and this one is a municipal housing provider.
48 of 120 units (40.0%) have two or more bedrooms, against a 35.0% minimum.
No minimum off-street parking applies citywide since June 2024; the option provides 30 vehicle and 220 bicycle spaces. Bicycle spaces are set by the Parking By-law at the development permit stage.
Meets the City's social housing definition: 30.0% of units for households below HILs (minimum 30.0%), owned by a city, secured for 60 years.
